definitions.type: function from natural numbers to real Euclidean spaces
definitions.definition: For each natural k, Rn(k)=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), the space of real k-tuples with distance (sum over j<k of |x_j-y_j|^2)^(1/2), with its standard Borel measurable structure. Rn(0) is the one-point space.
I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}, with the usual real metric.

definitions.type: subset of the metric product Rn(n)×ℝ
definitions.definition: Fmax=E×I. The ambient product distance between (x,t) and (y,u) is max(dist(x,y),|t-u|); use the Borel measurable structure.

definitions.type: family of coordinate maps Rn(k)×ℝ→Rn(k+1) indexed by natural k
definitions.definition: YuiJoinEquiv(k)(x,t)=(t,x_0,...,x_(k-1)) in Euclidean coordinates. This is the map defined in basis-registry.json /lean_header: identify Rn(k) with real Fin k-tuples using PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv, product with the real identity, swap factors, apply Fin.consEquivL, then the inverse PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv in dimension k+1. Its coordinate bijection is defined also at k=0; continuous linear equivalence and dimension preservation are to be justified in the metric-transfer inference, not assumed as new hypotheses.

Feuc=YuiJoinEquiv(n)''Fmax, the image of E×I in Euclidean (n+1)-space with the interval coordinate first. The interval-last realization requested by the original product notation is obtained by the coordinate permutation (t,x_0,...,x_(n-1))↦(x_0,...,x_(n-1),t).

definitions.type: unnormalized Hausdorff outer measure H^a(A) with values in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z, subset C⊆Z and real exponent a≥0, H^a(C) is the unnormalized Hausdorff outer measure with diameter-power cost: supremum over extended scales r>0 of the infimum, over countable covers C⊆⋃_i U_i with extended diameters ediam(U_i)≤r, of Σ_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty}(ediam(U_i))^a. Here ediam is the supremum of pairwise extended distances, with ediam(∅)=0. The inner supremum is zero for an empty member. For a>0 the cost is simply Σ_i(ediam(U_i))^a. No ball-volume or exponent-dependent normalization is included. The notation H^a(C) denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a C in the frozen basis.

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an extended metric space, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a subset C of an extended metric space Z, dimH C is its Hausdorff dimension: the infimum of positive real exponents a for which H^a(C)=0, embedded in [0,∞], with infimum of the empty set equal to ∞. In particular the empty set has dimension zero. This is the Hausdorff critical exponent convention of the frozen Mathlib dimH. A definition alone does not supply measure-dimension comparison theorems.

For real v, ofReal v is max(v,0) embedded into the extended nonnegative reals. Nonnegative real exponents and the real constant 1 in dimension inequalities are embedded this way. The dimension codomain [0,∞] has its usual extended order and addition.

inputs.statement: Let n be an arbitrary natural number, E⊆Euclidean n-space be nonempty and compact, I=[0,1], Fmax=E×I with the max product metric, and Feuc the coordinate realization of E×I with the Euclidean metric in dimension n+1. These are the original target hypotheses, including n=0.
For every n∈ℕ and nonempty compact E⊆Euclidean n-space, its Hausdorff dimension is a finite nonnegative value D, so dimH E=ofReal D in [0,∞].

binders.type: existentially quantified nonnegative finite real representative of dimH E

inputs.statement: For every Borel extended metric space X, A⊆X and d≥0: dimH A<d implies H^d(A)=0; d<dimH A implies H^d(A)=∞; H^d(A)≠∞ implies dimH A≤d; and H^d(A)=∞ implies d≤dimH A. Exponents are nonnegative reals embedded in [0,∞] in dimension comparisons.

locals.declaration: Choose the representative D≥0 with dimH E=ofReal D from N001 for H001.
Fix an arbitrary real s, with 0<s<D introduced as the local antecedent L2.
Define sstar=(D+max(0,(dimH Fmax).toReal-1))/2, using the total real-value map.

argument.text: Use H001 and choose the real representative D from N001. Temporarily assume L1: dimH E>0, the additional antecedent in the exported conclusion. Since D≥0 and dimH E=ofReal D, this gives D>0. Rn(n) is a second countable universe-0 metric space with its Borel structure: rational-coordinate boxes form a countable base when n>0, and the singleton space has a finite base when n=0. A countable base of rectangles shows that its max product with ℝ has the product Borel structure and is a Borel metric space.

produces.statement: D>0, dimH E=ofReal D, and Rn(n) is a second countable universe-0 Borel metric space whose max product with ℝ is a Borel metric space.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary real s and temporarily assume L2: 0<s<D. F001 yields ofReal s<dimH E. Also s+1>0.

produces.statement: s>0, s+1>0 and ofReal s<dimH E.

argument.text: Apply the second implication of E003 to X=Rn(n), A=E and exponent s. The strict inequality in F002 proves H^s(E)=∞.
Apply E020 to X=Rn(n), A=E and s. Its premises follow from F001 and F002, and it gives H^s(E)≤H^(s+1)(Fmax). By F003 the left side is infinity, so H^(s+1)(Fmax)=∞ in the extended nonnegative reals.

Apply the fourth implication of E003 in the Borel max product to Fmax at exponent s+1. From F004 obtain ofReal(s+1)≤dimH Fmax. Discharge L2 and universally close s, retaining only L1: for every real s with 0<s<D this lower bound holds.

produces.statement: For every real sbound with 0<sbound<D, ofReal(sbound+1)≤dimH Fmax.

binders.type: real exponent universally bound in this fact

argument.text: Define sstar=(D+max(0,(dimH Fmax).toReal-1))/2. Temporarily assume L3: dimH Fmax<ofReal(D+1). Then dimH Fmax is finite, its real representative is nonnegative and strictly less than D+1, and max(0,(dimH Fmax).toReal-1)<D because D>0. The midpoint definition implies 0<sstar<D and (dimH Fmax).toReal<sstar+1. Consequently dimH Fmax<ofReal(sstar+1), contradicting F005 at sstar. Discharging L3 proves ofReal(D+1)≤dimH Fmax. By F001, ofReal(D+1)=dimH E+1. Discharge L1 to prove precisely the conditional lower bound in the exported conclusion, and universally close the original n,E. No assumption of positive ambient dimension or finiteness of dimH Fmax was used outside the contradiction branch; the representative D has been eliminated from the output.
